To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NH4+ inhibits 13NO3--influx, but that NH4+ also increases 13NO3-efflux.
NH4+ inhibits 13NO3--uptake by barley (Hordeun vulgare) by inhibiting the high-affinity NO3- transporter, and that the inhibition is most pronounced at low external NO2- or NO3-.

(1) NH4+ inhibition is mediated via the inducible, high-affinity transport component; (2) NH4+ reduces NO3- influx and increases NO3- efflix; (3) the reduction in NO3- influx contributes most to the observed reduction in net uptake of NO; (4) NH4+ effects are more pronounced in plants induced with NO2-, than those induced with NO3-.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of NH4 on the NO3- uptake system in barley roots.
the effects of ammonium on the uptake and assimilation of nitrate in barley roots.
understanding the mechanisms of nitrate uptake in barley roots and how this process is inhibited by ammonium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exposure of barley roots to NH4+ reduces the influx of 13NO3-.
NH4+ inhibited the uptake of NO3- by plant roots via inhibition of influx and stimulation of efflux.
the inhibition of NO3- influx by NH4+ is mediated by a reduction of the inducible NO3- transport system and that this reduction is mediated by a combination of effects on influx and efflux.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NH4+ inhibits NO3- influx and stimulates efflux of NO3- by a process that is mediated via effects on NO3- transporters.
NH4+ inhibits the uptake of 13NO3-, and this effect is mediated by the inducible component of the high-affinity transport process.

NH4+ inhibits NO3- influx, but not by a simple block at the plasma membrane, and that the effect is mediated via effects of NH4+, or a metabolite, on the inducibility of NO3- uptake and/or on the activity of NO3- transport systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NH4+ can inhibit NO3- absorption by reducing the rate of NO3- influx, and that this inhibition is mediated via the high-affinity NO3- uptake system.
the inhibition of 13NO3--uptake by 1 mM NH+4 is not due to a direct effect on the plasma membrane.
the inhibition of NO3- uptake is due primarily to a reduction of influx, and not to an increase in efflux, as has been suggested by other studies.
